title: acceptance: exempt has a complete read path and no writer -- the only assignment in the workspace is inside a test
body:
**`acceptance: exempt` HAS A COMPLETE READ PATH AND NO WRITER. A TEST PINS THE SEMANTICS OF A STATE NO USER CAN REACH.**

Reported from OUTSIDE this estate by lamplight-vc, re-driven here 2026-09-03 before filing.

## The measurement

`AcceptanceMode::Exempt` is assigned in exactly ONE place in the entire workspace:

    native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/contract.rs:988
      #[test]
      fn exempt_is_announced_never_inferred() {
        t.acceptance = Some(crate::model::AcceptanceMode::Exempt);

**That is a test.** `grep -rn 'AcceptanceMode::Exempt' native/rust/crates/ | grep -v '/tests/'` returns that line and nothing else.

## The read path is fully built

- `contract.rs:464` -- `gate()` returns `Verdict::Exempt` when `thread.acceptance.is_some()`, ahead of every other check.
- `contract.rs:434` -- renders as `EXEMPT`.
- `contract.rs:446` -- counts as a pass.
- `doctor.rs:293` -- deliberately NOT folded in with `Pass`, with a comment explaining why.
- `mcp.rs:1286` -- `Verdict::Exempt { .. } => "exempt"`.

## The write path does not exist

`intent ac` offers list, status, satisfy, unsatisfy, gate, descope, rescope, withdraw, reinstate, new, edit. `intent at` offers list, lint, green, red, na, new, edit. **Neither carries a verb or a flag that sets `acceptance`.** Nothing in `surface/dispatch-table.json` names it.

## Why the test makes it worse rather than better

The test is called `exempt_is_announced_never_inferred`, and it is correct: exemption SHOULD be announced rather than deduced from an empty criteria list. **But there is no door to announce it through.** So the test asserts a discipline about a transition that cannot occur, passes forever, and reads to anyone auditing coverage as evidence that the feature works. **A green test over an unreachable state is the strongest possible disguise for a missing writer** -- it is the `IN-AG-RED-CONTROL-001` failure at feature scope: the test cannot go red for the reason that matters, because the state it guards can only be produced by the test itself.

## Live cost, outside this estate

lamplight-vc reports it blocking three Lamplight work packages: a thread that genuinely has no acceptance criteria cannot declare itself exempt, so its gate stays BLOCKED and the WPs cannot close. **The estate that wrote the feature does not feel this, because nothing here has needed to announce an exemption yet.**

## Not claimed

Which door is right -- `intent st exempt <ID> --reason`, a flag on `st new`, or a field on `st edit`. **Whether exemption needs a recorded reason is the real design question**, and `Verdict::Exempt` already carries a `Detail::Diagnosis`, which suggests it was meant to. Also not claimed: that no other estate has hit this; nobody has asked.
